Reviewers disagree on severity: openai_gpt-6-luna says MAJOR (confidence 5); anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash say NIT (confidence 2). The NIT reviewers say the failure does not map to this PR's diff: the file is not in PR CHANGED FILES, `sandbox_solc_resolve_versions` returns immediately when `SANDBOX_SOLC_VERSIONS` is unset, and issue #9199 already tracks it. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 suggests re-running the shard on head 6ea36343 and on merge-base 507ba62a, and treating it as this PR's defect only if it passes on the base.

  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The third-party Copilot reviewer stops before analysing any code because its instruction payload is too large.
  WHY: The check-run fails with exit 1 whatever the diff contains; the PR edits neither AGENTS.md nor CLAUDE.md (it adds only agents.d fragments), so nothing in PR CHANGED FILES can fix it.
- (third-party check, no code site):copilot-pull-request-reviewer check-run, HTTP 422 `custom_instructions_too_large` | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The Copilot reviewer fails before analysing any code because its custom-instruction payload (AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md) is over its limit.
  WHY: The reviewer tool rejects its own prompt size before the review request is created; this PR adds only agents.d/ fragments (the mechanism the repo mandates), so no file in this PR can fix it. This is likely the same check-run issue as the CLAUDE.md entry above, but it is kept separate because the cited file differs.
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:587-611 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `resolve_ci_reissue_base_branch` assumes `RETARGET_MERGED_BASE_ENABLED=true` is always enough for `retarget_merged_base.sh` to work when following a deleted integration branch.
  WHY: If the helper fails because of a missing dependency in the environment (git config or git binary), the resolver reports `branch_lookup_failed`, which may hide the root cause; diagnosis then depends on the operator reading the helper's stderr.
